Find endmembers from a list of lead isotope data points.

Source: R/ASTR_PbIso_endmembers.R
pb_iso_endmembers.Rd

Finds endmembers from a set of lead isotope data using principal component analysis and the geochron slope according to the two-stage model by Stacy and Kramers (1975), following the process outlined in Shnyr et al. (2026).

Usage

pb_iso_endmembers(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ASTR'
pb_iso_endmembers(
  x,
  tolerance = c(0.01, 0.01),
  clamp = c(Inf, Inf),
  geo_slope = 0.626208,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

ASTR object containing 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, and 208Pb/204Pb isotope ratios.

...

Additional parameters

tolerance

Vector of length two, with corresponding tolerance values for group 1 and group 2 for points considered to lie on the respective geochron lines, default is c(0.01, 0.01).

clamp

Limit filter for points away from the principal component end based on Euclidean distance, default is c(Inf, Inf).

geo_slope

Whole number value of geo-chron slope, Default value is 0.626208

Value

An ASTR object with additional class attribute ASTR_Pbiso_endmembr. The output extends the input table in x with a column end_membr, which stores the estimated endmember groups.

Endmember groups consist of group1, group2, and groupmix. groupmix represents the values along the mixing line.

References

Shnyr, E., Kuflik, T., Desai, K., and Eshel, T. (2026) Determining the origins of Phoenician silver: Exploring the potential of machine learning for lead isotope analysis. Journal of Archaeological Science 188, pp. 106–499. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2026.106499

Stacey, J. S., & Kramers, J. D. (1975). Approximation of Terrestrial Lead Isotope Evolution by a Two-Stage Model. Earth and Planetry Science Letters, 26, 207–221.

See also

Other Pb isotope functions: age_models, as_pbiso_ref_data(), geom_sk_lines(), pb_iso_prov_dist(), pb_iso_prov_predict(), pb_iso_train_data(), tel_dor

Examples

# example code
pb_iso_endmembers(tel_dor)
#> Warning: PC2 or PC3 are not normally distributed. This may indicate that the variation is not random noise.
#> ASTR table
#> Analytical columns: 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb
#> Contextual columns: end_membr 
#> # A data frame: 32 × 5
#>       ID `206Pb/204Pb` `207Pb/204Pb` `208Pb/204Pb` end_membr
#>    <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>    
#>  1     1          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  2     2          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  3     3          19.0          15.7          39.1 group2   
#>  4     4          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  5     5          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  6     6          17.9          15.6          38.0 group1   
#>  7     7          17.9          15.6          38.0 groupmix 
#>  8     8          17.9          15.6          38.0 group1   
#>  9     9          17.9          15.6          38.0 group1   
#> 10    10          19.0          15.7          39.4 group2   
#> # ℹ 22 more rows

# No clamping
no_clamp <- pb_iso_endmembers(tel_dor)
#> Warning: PC2 or PC3 are not normally distributed. This may indicate that the variation is not random noise.
no_clamp[no_clamp$end_membr == "group2", ]
#> ASTR table
#> Analytical columns: 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb
#> Contextual columns: end_membr 
#> # A data frame: 12 × 5
#>       ID `206Pb/204Pb` `207Pb/204Pb` `208Pb/204Pb` end_membr
#>    <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>    
#>  1     1          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  2     2          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  3     3          19.0          15.7          39.1 group2   
#>  4     4          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  5     5          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  6    10          19.0          15.7          39.4 group2   
#>  7    24          18.9          15.7          38.9 group2   
#>  8    26          19.0          15.7          39.1 group2   
#>  9    27          19.0          15.7          39.1 group2   
#> 10    29          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#> 11    30          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#> 12    31          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   

# Clamping reduces the group size by distance from the principal endmember
clamp <- pb_iso_endmembers(tel_dor, clamp = c(Inf, 0.1))
#> Warning: PC2 or PC3 are not normally distributed. This may indicate that the variation is not random noise.
#> Warning: Endmember group has less than two points. The likelihood of a point being an endmember is low.
clamp[clamp$end_membr == "group2", ]
#> ASTR table
#> Analytical columns: 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb
#> Contextual columns: end_membr 
#> # A data frame: 1 × 5
#>      ID `206Pb/204Pb` `207Pb/204Pb` `208Pb/204Pb` end_membr
#>   <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>    
#> 1    10          19.0          15.7          39.4 group2   

# Reducing tolerance values narrows the grouping around the geochron
pb_iso_endmembers(tel_dor, tolerance = c(0.001, 0.001))
#> Warning: PC2 or PC3 are not normally distributed. This may indicate that the variation is not random noise.
#> ASTR table
#> Analytical columns: 206Pb/204Pb, 207Pb/204Pb, 208Pb/204Pb
#> Contextual columns: end_membr 
#> # A data frame: 32 × 5
#>       ID `206Pb/204Pb` `207Pb/204Pb` `208Pb/204Pb` end_membr
#>    <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>    
#>  1     1          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  2     2          19.0          15.7          39.0 groupmix 
#>  3     3          19.0          15.7          39.1 groupmix 
#>  4     4          19.0          15.7          39.0 groupmix 
#>  5     5          19.0          15.7          39.0 group2   
#>  6     6          17.9          15.6          38.0 group1   
#>  7     7          17.9          15.6          38.0 groupmix 
#>  8     8          17.9          15.6          38.0 groupmix 
#>  9     9          17.9          15.6          38.0 group1   
#> 10    10          19.0          15.7          39.4 group2   
#> # ℹ 22 more rows
